title: Away from the knot's law, counting on the knot's spaces is #P-hard
claim: Counting on the knot's spaces (connected non-2-colourable cubic triple systems) with weight lam per monochromatic line is #P-hard under Turing reductions at every coupling lam0 not in {1, -3} at which some atom has alpha + beta != 0 and rho^2 of infinite order: from a plain system G with Pfaffian incidence graph and a Pfaffian negation set O, the knot's spaces G_ij (2i atoms on each incidence off O, 2j + 1 on O) give Q(rho^2i, rho^2j), and bivariate interpolation returns #col(G) (Theorem 4 of PLAIN-COUNT-20261031-001A). With ticket A this covers every real lam0 outside {0, 1, -1, -3}, and the same holds with one line deleted (deficiency one). The excluded couplings are polynomial on knot's spaces: lam = 0 (zero; with one line deleted, Theorem 1 of the note), 1, -1 (a quadratic exponential sum over GF(2)), oo (linear algebra) and -3 ((-2)^n |det|, the dimer coupling). Checked end to end: #col of two planar and one non-planar Pfaffian source recovered exactly from counts of knot's spaces at real, negative and complex couplings, with Fano and splice atoms, and from deficiency-one knot's spaces. Deficiency one at lam = -3 is left open.
failure_conditions: A recovered colouring count that differs from the true count, or an oracle instance that is colourable or disconnected.
A real coupling outside {0, 1, -1, -3} where every atom degenerates (contradicting ticket A).
A tractable-coupling algorithm that disagrees with the counter.
foundation_claim_scope: A complexity dichotomy for counting on the knot's spaces at real couplings; complex couplings are ticket C.

validation.status: checked: instances are knot's spaces; the oracle identity against a direct even-subgraph sum; six end-to-end recoveries (three sources, four couplings, two atoms) with an independent counter; deficiency one end to end; the tractable couplings by their algorithms; controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: the reduction pattern (gadget plus interpolation from a hard point) is standard; the dichotomy on the knot's spaces and its two singled-out couplings: no overlap found yet (literature check at closure)
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-31; the end-to-end code shares no code with ticket A.
